archetype.name: Game Manager (spot starter)
archetype.definition: A veteran backup who keeps the offense on schedule with short, accurate, low-risk throws and a little scrambling, but gives back too much to sacks and rarely pushes the ball downfield.

report.headline: A competent fill-in stint for Lamar, now ended by a toe injury
report.take:
Tyler Huntley is what he has been for six years in Baltimore and Miami: a high-percentage, short-area backup who protects the football and struggles to make the pocket work. With Lamar Jackson out, he started Weeks 5 through 7 and did his job. As a starter he posted +0.107 EPA per dropback with a 68% completion rate, a spot-start line that sits comfortably above the league-average passer's -0.002. His season completion rate of 69.1 ranks 6th of 49 and his 0.9% interception rate ranks 10th. The approach is plain: intended air yards of 6.69, throws that land 2.25 yards short of the sticks, and 81 of his 110 charted attempts under 10 air yards.

The efficiency didn't come from the short game, though. His throws under 10 yards added only +0.021 EPA each. The value came from 29 attempts at 10-plus air yards, at +0.5 a throw, and nearly all of that from 22 intermediate throws. That is a thin slice to carry a season, and it went mostly to Rashod Bateman and Josh Cuevas. His most-targeted pieces beyond Zay Flowers were a drain: Mark Andrews at -0.73 EPA per target and Justice Hill at -0.404. The middle of the field was a dead zone, 50% completions and a CPOE of -17.1.

The sacks are the part that isn't noise. A 9.1% sack rate ranks 37th of 49, and 39.3% of his pressures became sacks. Every season of his career shows the same pressure-to-sack habit, so this is who he is, not a slump. Holding the ball for 2.84 seconds while throwing short is the worst combination, and his scrambling didn't pay for it: nine scrambles, zero first downs. That is why his passing EPA total of +2.4 turns into -4.3 across all dropbacks. The accuracy was also a step down from last year's small-sample 12.9 CPOE: down 10 points, with his bad-throw rate up 6.9.

The arc closed badly. His bad-throw rate climbed from 9.7% in Week 5 to 23.5% by Week 7. Then came a Week 8 relief appearance in Buffalo: pressured on 80% of dropbacks, a lost fumble, and -9.3 EPA on four attempts. He went on injured reserve with a toe sprain on November 5, with an estimated return of February 15, 2027. He is listed as QB5. For practical purposes his 2026 is over, and the three-start sample is the record.

strengths.title: Ball security and completion rate
strengths.body: He completes passes at a top-10 clip and almost never throws it to the other team, the product of a quick, short-first read structure. It is backed by his career: zero interceptions in 2025 and consistently high completion ranks. This is the trait that makes him a viable spot starter.

strengths.title: Efficient as the actual starter
strengths.body: In his three starts the offense functioned. Per-dropback EPA was solidly positive and the passing EPA averaged 3.8 a game, so the Ravens weren't sunk by his play in that stretch. The season-wide numbers are dragged down by a mop-up cameo, not the starts.

strengths.title: Intermediate throws drove the value
strengths.body: His 10-19 yard throws produced +0.61 EPA apiece, by far his best range, largely to Bateman and Cuevas. On 22 attempts that is a hint rather than a skill read, and the 54.5% completion rate there says some of it was a few big hits.

concerns.title: Sacks are a career-long habit
concerns.body: He turns pressure into sacks at one of the worst rates in the league, and has every year of his career. Holding the ball nearly three seconds while throwing short of the sticks means the hold isn't buying downfield shots. The scrambles that should offset it produced no first downs, which is why his dropback EPA ends up negative.

concerns.title: Accuracy slipped from 2025
concerns.body: Last year's CPOE was an outlier on four games, and this year gave much of it back, with the bad-throw rate climbing week to week. A 17.3% bad-throw rate ranking 38th of 42 fits his 2021 and 2023 profiles more than his 2025 one.

concerns.title: No middle of the field, no deep ball
concerns.body: Throws over the middle were his worst area, and he completed one of seven deep attempts. Andrews, a middle-of-the-field target, was a heavy negative in his hands. Without the seam and the deep shot, defenses can squat on the boundary short game.

trend.note: His best football came in the Week 5 win at Atlanta. The bad throws then mounted through Cleveland and Cincinnati, and he ended with a disastrous relief cameo in Buffalo. The last-three line runs below his season on CPOE and sack rate.

nextGame.headline: He won't play; on IR with a toe sprain
nextGame.body:
Huntley is on injured reserve with a toe sprain and an estimated return of February 15, 2027, and the depth chart has him fifth. He will not face the Chargers. For context, this would have been a mixed setup for his style. The Chargers allow little on short throws, ranking 11th on short-pass EPA, but bleed on deep shots, 29th, and Huntley rarely throws deep. The Ravens are 5.5-point favorites in a 38.5 total, largely because Los Angeles has the league's worst offense by EPA.

The availability that matters is on the Ravens' side. Lamar Jackson is on IR after thumb surgery, with a December 13 target and a stated plan to return, and Joe Fagnano started Week 9. Justin Herbert is questionable with a finger injury that avoided a fracture, which bears on Baltimore's game script more than on anything Huntley controls.

keyMatchups.title: His own IR status
keyMatchups.body: The toe sprain put him on injured reserve on November 5. The estimated return date falls after the regular season, so any role this year would require a much faster recovery than projected.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers punish short, leak deep
keyMatchups.body: The defense is stingy on short throws and generous downfield, the opposite of what a checkdown-first passer wants. It's mostly relevant to whoever starts for Baltimore.

nextGame.watch: Whether the Ravens move him further down the chain or keep him on IR all year, and when Lamar Jackson's December return target firms up.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is that Huntley doesn't play again in 2026. He is on IR with an estimated return after the regular season, sits fifth on the depth chart, and Lamar Jackson is targeting a December return. If the toe heals faster and injuries force him back into a start, expect the same profile his career and this season agree on. He would complete a high share of short passes and rarely throw interceptions, but take too many sacks and produce little downfield.

In a hypothetical start I'd project roughly 150-210 passing yards with a sack rate around 8-10%. The intermediate efficiency from his three starts is the piece most likely to regress on a larger sample. The sack problem and ball security are the parts that will hold.
swingFactors: Speed of his toe recovery versus the February estimate
Whether Baltimore's QB chain thins out further

confidence.note: On IR, return estimated post-season; profile matches six years of career data.
